description: Shared M4 Slice 1 navigation operation cases, run by navigation_tests.rs (native, database half) and navigationParity.test.ts (browser/test twin on node:sqlite and sql.js). $A and $B stand for two 64-hex content hashes. Materials 'mat' and 'other' exist in every case. A step with 'sql' runs that statement directly between operations. 'final.tuple' is [page, label, confirmed_read, origin hash, status, owner generation].

cases.name: strict decoding refuses every malformed request before any transaction
labels at the limits: 100 code points and a zero-width space inside are accepted; Unicode trimming agrees
titles count code points, not UTF-16 units
reservations are increasing; a supersede cancels the earlier token in the same step
a supersede must name an issued token
reservation refuses overflow without changing the claim
reservation starts above a saved owner even without a claim row
an unknown material cannot reserve
an ignored claim write issues no token and changes nothing (R38)
setup: CREATE TRIGGER ignore_claim BEFORE INSERT ON material_operation_claims BEGIN SELECT RAISE(IGNORE); END

cases.name: a claim write that is blocked issues no token (R33)
setup: CREATE TRIGGER block_claim BEFORE UPDATE ON material_operation_claims BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'blocked'); END

cases.name: a claim that persists the wrong token fails closed and rolls back (R38)
setup: CREATE TRIGGER skew AFTER INSERT ON material_operation_claims BEGIN UPDATE material_operation_claims SET reserved_generation = 99 WHERE material_id = NEW.material_id; END

cases.name: cancelling an older token is a no-op; an unissued one is refused
only the exact current token commits the whole tuple, unconfirmed and active (R34)
a commit with no claim is refused and writes nothing
a token never reserved is refused
once a later token exists the earlier one is refused and the winner's tuple stands
a cancelled token is refused at commit
commit needs a recorded identity
commit refuses other content
commit refuses a page past the trusted count, never clamping
a replayed commit is refused
a commit whose write fails rolls back and keeps the saved tuple
setup: CREATE TRIGGER fail_update BEFORE UPDATE ON material_reading_state BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'disk'); END

cases.name: a new request resets read confirmation
read confirmation and clearing apply to exactly the saved request named
a held confirmation or clear for content A at the same page cannot touch content B (M4S1-R1)

op.sql: UPDATE material_content_identities SET content_sha256 = '$B' WHERE material_id = 'mat'

cases.name: a held confirmation from an older generation of the same content and page is stale (M4S1-R1)
a saved place with an unknown origin stays unverified and cannot be confirmed
setup: INSERT INTO material_reading_state VALUES ('mat', 2, NULL, 0, NULL, 'unverified', 3, 'x')
INSERT INTO material_bookmarks (id, material_id, page_index, originating_content_sha256, title, status, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('old', 'mat', 1, NULL, 'Old', 'unverified', 'x', 'x')

cases.name: a drifted saved place cannot be confirmed
bookmarks need the named, recorded content and an in-range page; ids are unique
a held bookmark for replaced content is refused (M4S1-R1)

op.sql: UPDATE material_content_identities SET content_sha256 = '$B' WHERE material_id = 'mat'

cases.name: bookmarks are limited per material
setup: WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 500) INSERT INTO material_bookmarks (id, material_id, page_index, originating_content_sha256, title, created_at, updated_at) SELECT 'seed' || i, 'mat', 1, '$A', 't', 'x', 'x' FROM n

cases.name: another material's bookmark cannot be deleted from here
setup: INSERT INTO material_bookmarks (id, material_id, page_index, originating_content_sha256, title, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('b1', 'mat', 1, '$A', 't', 'x', 'x')

cases.name: read returns identity, state and bookmarks in page order
setup: INSERT INTO material_bookmarks (id, material_id, page_index, originating_content_sha256, title, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('b1', 'mat', 9, '$A', 't', 'x', 'x'), ('b2', 'mat', 1, '$A', 't', 'x', 'x')
